summary:
Research product advancing unit-claim-heartbeat-header-gate from obligation to a constructible check; preflight-validated with valid=True and no diagnostics.

New decisive evidence recorded: the transport callback body is exactly a call into processHeartbeat. integ_test.go:561-583 installs a custom heartbeat handler that inspects rpc.Command.(*AppendEntriesRequest) and, for heartbeats it does not suppress, calls r.processHeartbeat(rpc) — a library-authored demonstration that a direct handler invocation is the production seam, not a synthetic shortcut. Reachability is also bounded: the fast path exists only for a Transport that invokes the callback. net_transport does (net_transport.go:724-733), while InmemTransport.SetHeartbeatHandler is a documented no-op (inmem_transport.go:72-75), so an in-process cluster test never exercises the bypass. And raft_test.go:3160-3200 with the skipStartup flag (config.go:243-244, api.go:618) gives the sanctioned way to drive request handlers on a node whose background goroutines are not running.

Consequence for method: this turns the fast-path question into a concrete, race-free check design — build a node with skipStartup, drive the same out-of-window pure heartbeat through processRPC (expect ErrUnsupportedProtocol and no state change) and through processHeartbeat (observe whether term/state/leader/lastContact change), with the net_transport classification declared as a sourced premise rather than reproduced over TCP.

Map change (base version 5): the existing behavior b-heartbeat-fast-path gains two sources and one branch note constraining its reachability; no meaning, identity, edge, requirement or previously accepted Surface changed, so the confirmed ConfigurationStore violation and all accepted results keep their original basis.

Still open and explicitly unresolved: whether an out-of-window peer can deliver a pure heartbeat in a legal deployment, the election consequence via lastContact refresh, and whether the omission is deliberate design (in which case the correct disposition is a documented assumption rather than a violation). No verdict claimed.
